Subject: Post-demo: BrightGrid inference comparison & p95/p99 test plan

Kerry — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum while your infra team evaluates: 

Summary of what we discussed:
- BrightGrid use case: real-time personalization (200–400 tokens per request), spiky traffic with 60–120s microbursts, strict p99 latency targets for in-session personalization.
- Competitive frame: you asked for apples-to-apples tests vs hyperscaler endpoints (AWS Bedrock/Vertex AI/HyperCloud) and a Redwood baseline (hosted + dedicated) so you can compare p95/p99 and sustained tokens/sec.

Proposed A/B / test matrix (short):
1) Hyperscaler endpoint (customer-chosen model) — baseline test from BrightGrid region.
2) Redwood Hosted (same open model) — default batching/quantization profile.
3) Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) — KV prefix caching enabled + aggressive batching policy.

Metrics to capture:
- p50/p95/p99 latency (warm and cold), tail latency heatmap
- tokens/sec sustained (5-min steady windows) and peak tokens/sec during microbursts
- success/error rate, connection churn, and memory/CPU utilization on client side

Immediate asks from BrightGrid (what we need from you):
- Confirm a 2–4 hour test window (we suggest Nov 30–Dec 1, 09:00–13:00 PST)
- Share a 200–400-token sample workload (prompts) and the expected request mix (we've attached a stub: brightgrid-sample-prompts.json)
- Add our test IPs to your allowlist (I include the IPs in my next message)
- Provide an infra contact for DocuSign/PO if we need an access exception for Dedicated testing (you mentioned procurement).

Operational notes / Redwood differentiators worth highlighting in the run:
- Dedicated mode will let you pin model binaries + enable prefix/KV caching for identical prefixes (realistic for personalization). That usually reduces p95 by 15–35% on these workloads versus stateless hyperscaler endpoints because of cache locality and continuous batching.
- We can run an extra pass that disables KV caching to show the delta.
- We’ll capture unit-cost per 1k tokens across configs so you can factor economics into the decision.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm test window + sample workload by EOD 11/29.
2) We run a short prep test (30–45m) to validate traffic shaping and allowlist.
3) Full A/B run with automated p95/p99 capture and an ops readout within 24h of the run.

Attachments: brightgrid-sample-prompts.json (sample prompt set), bench-runbook checklist (linked in follow-ups).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call with your infra lead to unblock the allowlist if helpful.

—Mina

Mina / Jonas — pulling together the bench approach so we have clear test prescriptions for BrightGrid's infra team. Quoting Kerry's note for context:

> Thanks Mina — that all looks sensible. We're keen to see the Dedicated vs hyperscaler delta for the p99 tail.

High-level test harness plan (internal):
- Workload shaping: replay BrightGrid's sample prompts (200–400 tokens) with a Pareto fan-out matching their reported request mix (70% short, 30% long). Burst profile: 60s ramp to target RPS, hold 90s microburst, then cool-down.
- Measurement windows: run 6 x 10-minute steady-state windows per config; compute p50/p95/p99 over each window and then report the median window values plus max across windows for tail awareness. Use 95/99 percentiles computed at request level including queuing latency.
- Configs to run:
  A) Hyperscaler (customer-chosen model, region)
  B) Redwood Hosted (standard batching, quantization X)
  C) Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) — variations: KV cache ON, KV cache OFF
- Concurrency mapping: we'll instrument to map concurrent open connections to observed tokens/sec; for the prep run include 50, 150, and 300 concurrent request simulators so we can derive tokens/sec curves.

Operational notes:
- Need HubSpot deal id (I used BG-2028-047) and a sandbox token with limited qps for the prep run.
- Attach runbook skeleton (bench-runbook.md) and a templated k6 script; we'll include a redwood-bench-skel.yaml for the full run.

If this looks good I'll prepare the orchestration job spec and the allowlist IPs for Mina to send — suggest we send those in the prep email so BrightGrid can add them before the prep window.

Rishi
